verdict.rationale: Atlassian publishes the Jira Cloud platform REST API as a versioned (v3) reference with a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.1 spec of 433 paths, plus a formal deprecation policy with a 6-month commitment. Community users independently describe driving Jira via REST queries and API wrapper scripts. The probe 404s only hit guessed root paths, while the spec is documented at its own URL, so they do not contradict this. Missing for 10: no evidence on authentication and rate-limit documentation for programmatic or agent clients, and the reference has no in-page runnable console (only a Postman export).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Atlassian publishes the Jira Cloud platform REST API as a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.1 document (info title "The Jira Cloud platform REST API", 433 paths)
This documentation is for version 3 of the Jira Cloud platform REST API, which is the latest version.
a deprecated REST API in the cloud environment must remain available in its original form "for at least 6 months"
One of the things I like most about Jira is the ability to run useful queries via its REST API on the stored data.
